# SECTION 2: MIA

## Regression model - Logistic Regression

### Which method are you using?

State which method you are using.

### Missing values drop

Should you be dropping missing values for your technique? If so are there variables you should drop before dropping rows with missing values? Put the code and explanation here.

```{r}
gap |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x))))

gap_knnreg <- gap |> 
  select(-c(energy_use_per_person, cell_phones, happiness, disaster_deaths_per_100k, geo, name)) |> 
  drop_na()

```

### Making model

Make your regression model. Tune or feature select as suitable for your model.

```{r}

reg_metrics <- metric_set(mae, mse, rmse)

# Folds
set.seed(2005)
folds <- vfold_cv(gap_knnreg, v = 5)

# Recipe
knnreg_recipe <- recipe(murder_rate ~ ., data = gap_knnreg) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

# Specify the KNN model and mark 'neighbors' as tune()
knnreg_spec <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors=tune(), weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create a workflow
knnreg_wf<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(knnreg_recipe)|>
  add_model(knnreg_spec)

# Tuning grid
knnreg_grid <- tibble(neighbors = seq(from=1, to=15, by=2))

# Cross validation
knnreg_cv <- tune_grid(
  knnreg_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = knnreg_grid,
  metrics = reg_metrics
)
cv_metrics_knnreg<-collect_metrics(knnreg_cv)

# Plotting and finding the best k-nearest neighbors
autoplot(knnreg_cv, metric = "rmse")

best_k <- select_best(knnreg_cv, metric = "rmse")

# New specification using tuned k-nearest neighbors
knnreg_best_spec<-nearest_neighbor(neighbors=3,  weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn")|>
  set_mode("regression")

# New workflow for tuned k-nearest neighbors
knnreg_best_wf<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(knnreg_recipe)|>
  add_model(knnreg_best_spec)

# Fit the final model
knnreg_fit <- 
  knnreg_best_wf |> 
  fit(data = gap_knnreg)

```

## Classification model - Random Forest

### Which method are you using?

State which method you are using.

### Missing values drop

Should you be dropping missing values for your technique? If so are there variables you should drop before dropping rows with missing values? Put the code and explanation here.

```{r}
gap |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x))))

gap_rf <- gap |> 
  select(-c(energy_use_per_person, cell_phones, happiness, disaster_deaths_per_100k, geo, name)) |> 
  drop_na()
```

### Making model

Make your classification model. Tune or feature select as suitable for your model.

```{r}
rf_recipe=recipe(sexual_harassment ~ ., data = gap_rf) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

rf_spec <- rand_forest() |>
  set_mode("classification")|>
  set_engine("ranger",importance = "impurity") #Impurity here is sum of squares residual

rf_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)

rf_fit=rf_workflow |>
  fit(data = gap_rf)
```

### Which variables

Which variables are in your final model/are the most important in your model? Any surprises? Any concerns?

```{r}
importance_values <- rf_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |> 
  ranger::importance() 

importance_df=importance_values <- tibble(
  Variable = names(importance_values),
  Importance = importance_values
)

importance_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_flip() +  # Makes variables easy to read vertically
  labs(
    title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
    x = "Features",
    y = "Importance (Impurity reduction)"
  )
```

### Missing values drop

### Making clusters

```{r}
#Peform k-means clustering

set.seed(123)
kmeans4_spec<- k_means(num_clusters = 4) |>
  set_engine("stats")

kmeans4_rec<- recipe(~., data=gapminderCluster)

kmeans4_wf<-workflow()|>
  add_recipe(kmeans4_rec)|>
  add_model(kmeans4_spec)

kmeans4_fit <-kmeans4_wf|>
  fit(data = gapminder_train)

#need to figure out how to combine.
```
